*sighs deeply while smoothing down blue dress*

Mmm... are we sure about this code? Homie, this is handling people's money and credit cards. I've seen Bart make better decisions, and that's saying something.

## Critical Issues

**SQL Injection (Lines 97, 105-107, 122, 141-143, 176-177, 194-196)**
Oh my. This is everywhere. `GetOrder`, `CancelOrder`, `GetUserOrders`, `ProcessRefund`, `ExportOrders` - all using string concatenation for queries. Anyone could type `'; DROP TABLE orders;--` and our whole family would be homeless.

**Storing Credit Cards in Plain Text (Lines 33, 73, 195)**
*Mmm-worried groan* We're storing full credit card numbers in the database AND returning them in API responses. This violates PCI-DSS. We'll lose our ability to process payments. Fix: Never store full card numbers. Use tokenization.

**Credit Card in Logs/Export (Lines 193-203)**
The export includes credit cards, and line 200's masking will panic on empty strings. Security breach waiting to happen.

## High Severity

**No Authentication/Authorization (All Handlers)**
Anyone can view, cancel, or refund ANY order. Line 93 lets users query other users' orders. I'll hold this team together, but I can't hold together customer trust after this.

**Race Condition in Inventory (Lines 64-70, 128-133)**
Fire-and-forget goroutines with no error handling. Payment charged but inventory reservation could silently fail. No rollback mechanism.

**Missing Error Handling Throughout**
Lines 41, 52, 59, 66, 83-85, 105, 129, 166 - all ignore errors from HTTP calls, JSON decoding, and database operations. If payment fails, we don't even know.

**Nil Pointer Dereference (Lines 59-60, 166-167)**
If HTTP calls fail, `resp` is nil. Accessing `resp.StatusCode` or `resp.Body` will crash the service.

## Medium Severity

**Cache Without Mutex on Read (Lines 92-95)**
Writing uses mutex (missing actually - line 82 doesn't lock!), reading doesn't. Concurrent map access will panic.

**Floating Point for Money (Lines 27, 46-48)**
Float64 for currency causes rounding errors. Use integer cents or decimal type.

**Response Body Not Closed (Lines 59, 83, 166)**
Memory leak. Always `defer resp.Body.Close()`.

**Loop Variable Capture (Lines 128-133)**
Classic Go bug. `productID` and `quantity` captured by reference, will have wrong values when goroutine executes.

## Low Severity

**No Request Timeouts (All HTTP Calls)**
External services hanging will exhaust connections.

**No Pagination Limit Validation (Line 138)**
Users could request limit=999999999.

**No Input Validation (Line 41)**
Empty orders, negative quantities, negative prices all accepted.

---

*straightens pearls firmly*

Homie, please focus on the backlog - this code needs a complete rewrite before it touches production. "Works in staging" doesn't mean it's safe when real attackers and real money are involved. I'm sending this back. The kids need college funds, and we can't afford the lawsuits this would cause.
